concept.name: Ultimate oscillator
concept.definition: Larry Williams' three-timeframe momentum oscillator (1976; Stocks & Commodities, 1985): a weighted blend (4:2:1) of buying-pressure-to-true-range ratios over 7, 14, and 28 periods, designed to reduce the false divergences of single-timeframe oscillators.
concept.intuition: Short-term momentum dominates the blend but is checked by two longer frames, so a divergence must show weakness across multiple horizons to count.
concept.mechanics: BP = Close - min(Low, prior Close); TR = max(High, prior Close) - min(Low, prior Close); Average_k = sum(BP, k)/sum(TR, k) for k = 7, 14, 28; UO = 100 x (4xAvg7 + 2xAvg14 + Avg28)/7. Williams' buy signal: a bullish divergence whose oscillator low is below 30, confirmed by a break above the divergence high.
concept.formula: UO = 100 x (4 x Avg7 + 2 x Avg14 + 1 x Avg28) / (4+2+1), with Avg_k = sum(BP, k) / sum(TR, k).
concept.failure_modes: The fixed 4:2:1 weighting and divergence-plus-level rules are intricate but still whipsaw; on quiet securities the oscillator may never reach 30 or 70 with default settings, inviting parameter fiddling.
concept.misconceptions: Despite the name it is not 'ultimate' or proven superior - it is one multi-frame weighting scheme among many, and its signals still require confirmation.
